intent:
Pull must be able to converge what Drift measures. detectProfileDrift compares SOUL/AGENTS/USER/MEMORY unconditionally; fileHash returns null for a missing file while contentHash('# User
') is a real digest, so a profile with no USER.md on disk is PERMANENTLY drifted. profile-pull writes those columns only when the file exists, so Pull can never clear them; only Push can, which is why the banner's own CTA says Push all. QA saw Pull all visibly work (a profile's skills count went 183 to 218) while the drift banner persisted. Guard each comparison with existsSync, exactly as the config.yaml branch already does. No behaviour change for files that DO exist: a genuinely differing file must still report drift. Source: the operator's live Hermes QA pass on dev@43d16c30, 2026-08-26; root cause traced and independently re-verified. Not a regression from the consolidation work. Closed 2026-08-26. The eight unconditional comparisons (four in detectProfileDrift, four in detectRootDrift, HERMES.md being the fifth and already guarded) collapsed into one predicate, fileDiffers(path, dbContent) = existsSync(path) && fileHash(path) !== contentHash(dbContent). The design question the task posed is answered SILENT and argued at length in the module header and below: an absent file reports nothing. The two things it would have been tempting to fix in passing and were not are recorded under deferred.
invariants: I1 A file that genuinely DIFFERS still reports drift. This is the invariant the task named and it is the one a careless fix destroys, because a guard that returns early satisfies every absent-file assertion while disabling drift outright. Proved two ways rather than asserted. Four of the eight oracle cases are differing-file cases over exactly the fields the fix touches (profile SOUL/AGENTS/USER/MEMORY, root SOUL/AGENTS/USER/MEMORY, root HERMES.md), and they were green before the fix and are green after. Then the predicate was mutated in place to `existsSync(path) && false && ...` and re-run: 3 failed, 5 passed. The three that died are the three differing-file cases. A test suite that survives that mutation is not testing drift.

I2 A file that is absent from disk reports no drift. Profile and root, all four markdown files each, with and without the memories/ directory existing. Measured before: detectProfileDrift on a root holding only SOUL.md, AGENTS.md and config.yaml returned fields ['config.yaml','USER.md','MEMORY.md']; it now returns ['config.yaml'].

I3 Pull converges the banner. The end-to-end case is the operator's QA report as an assertion: seed a profile whose disk has SOUL.md, AGENTS.md and config.yaml and no memories/, edit SOUL.md on disk, run pullProfileFromHermes with reconcileDisk, and ask for drift. Before: fields ['USER.md','MEMORY.md'], drifted true, for ever, whatever Pull did. After: fields [], drifted false.

I4 What Pull writes is unchanged. src/modules/hermes/lib/profile-pull.ts is not in this diff. Pull still writes soulMd, agentsMd, userMd and memoryMd only when the file exists; teaching it to create missing files is the larger design call the task fenced off, and the convergence in I3 is achieved by making Drift honest rather than by making Pull write more.

I5 No check is weakened. design-lint stays at 0 in 0 files across all eleven rules, no coverage floor moves, no existing assertion is removed or relaxed, and the two existing drift assertions in tests/unit/hermes-profile-sync.test.ts and tests/unit/profiles-api.test.ts still pass untouched. The suite only grows: 8 new cases, 0 deleted.

I6 The public contract is unchanged. ProfileDriftEntry, RootDriftEntry and FullDriftReport keep their exact shape, so GET /api/agent/profiles/sync/drift and deriveSyncStatus in src/app/api/agent/profiles/route.ts see the same fields they saw before, carrying fewer false entries. No new field, no ADR, no consumer to migrate.
oracle_provenance: Authored by the executor in this session BEFORE any production file was opened for edit, per the EXECUTOR R2 clause, and committed on its own at 1540f7d7 ahead of the implementation. One file, tests/unit/hermes-drift-missing-files.test.ts, run against the unfixed tree first: 4 failed, 4 passed, 8 total. That run is the freeze point and the four failures are quoted with their measured field arrays in the oracle commit message. The construction rule the file states in its own header and follows without exception: no absent-file case stands without a differing-file case over the same field, because a test that only proves 'absent means no drift' also passes when drift detection is deleted. The four PASSING cases in the frozen run are therefore the load-bearing half, and the mutation run under I1 is what shows they are load-bearing rather than decorative. One weakness to declare: the oracle exercises detectProfileDrift and detectRootDrift directly and does not drive the banner, so it proves the count the banner reads is right and does not prove the banner renders it. That seam is covered by tests/unit/profiles-api.test.ts, which was run and is green, and no further.
decision_absent_is_silent: The task asked whether 'missing on disk' should be silent or should be named as a different kind of drift. Ruled SILENT, and the argument is that it was never a signal in the first place. Nobody designed 'missing shows as drift'; it fell out of `null !== hash`. It arrived in the one field the banner renders, indistinguishable from a real difference, and being indistinguishable is precisely what made the true signal unreadable during the QA pass that raised this task: the operator ran Pull all, watched a profile's skills go 183 to 218, and had no way to tell the still-lit banner apart from a pull that had done nothing. Removing it raises the information content of the banner rather than lowering it. The counter-argument is real and is recorded rather than dismissed: 'your disk is missing SOUL.md' is a true and actionable fact, and after this change the banner goes quiet on it. It is not smuggled in here because naming it honestly means a second banner state and a second CTA, since only Push can materialise a file that does not exist, and that is a UI decision with a UI owner and the same shape of design call as teaching Pull to create missing files. Both belong to whoever takes that pass, with this task's header as the argument to overturn or adopt. What is NOT deferred is the correctness half: the banner no longer claims a difference that does not exist.
rollback: One-command revert of this task's two commits, 1540f7d7 (oracle) and this one. No migration, no schema element, no new route, no dependency, no persisted state, no public contract change, and no file outside src/modules/hermes/lib/profile-drift.ts and tests/. Reverting restores the permanent-drift defect and the oracle reverts with it, which is correct: the oracle is written against the fixed contract and is designed to fail on the old code. Nothing else in the tree depends on fileDiffers.
deferred: detectSkillDrift (same file, unchanged) still compares fileHash against contentHash with no existsSync guard, so a skill row whose file is not on disk is drifted for ever by the same mechanism, and pullSkillFromHermes cannot clear it either: it returns 'Skill file not found on disk'. Left alone deliberately. The task names detectProfileDrift and detectRootDrift and nothing else, and the skill case is arguably NOT the same case: a catalog row with no file means the skill is not installed, which is a stronger and more useful claim than 'this profile has no USER.md', and pull already says so out loud instead of silently doing nothing. It should be ruled on rather than swept along with this fix.

The config.yaml branch keeps its `else if (expectedConfig.trim().length > 0)`, so a missing config.yaml with a non-empty assembled config still reports drift, and a Pull cannot obviously clear that either since assembleConfigYamlForProfile derives from columns rather than from the file. It is the boundary of the rule this task applies, not an oversight, and it is left exactly as found because changing it is a behaviour change the task did not ask for and no oracle here covers. Whoever picks up the skill case should look at this in the same pass.

The drift banner (src/components/profiles/ProfilesDriftBanner.tsx) still has one state and one CTA, 'Push all to Hermes', which now understates what the operator can do: after this fix a lit banner is genuinely convergeable by Pull as well. Outside this task's claims and left for the UI pass, together with the 'absent on disk' state argued above.
